subject.title: Design: Telegram isolated ingress holds per-chat lane for the entire agent turn — long turns block the group, then die at 25 min

question: Should Telegram isolated ingress release the per-chat/topic spool lane after durable handoff to session admission instead of after the full agent turn completes?
rationale: The source-level defect is clear, but the durable fix changes Telegram transport ordering, timeout semantics, duplicate/replay safety, and downstream session-admission ownership, so maintainers need to choose the contract before code repair.

options.title: Detach After Durable Handoff
options.body: Move the Telegram spool lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable session handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

options.title: Keep Lane Ownership And Tune Timeout
options.body: Preserve the current one-handler-per-lane model and only adjust timeout or user feedback, accepting that ordinary same-lane messages still cannot reach steering during a long turn.

options.title: Split Narrow Follow-Ups
options.body: Handle timeout visibility and collect starvation separately while leaving this issue as the owner decision for Telegram lane ownership.

recommendation.title: Detach After Durable Handoff
recommendation.body: Move the Telegram spool lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable session handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and have the most direct recent history across the related run-lifecycle and Telegram spooled-update work.
